Compared with the CC alloy, the average sizes of Cr particles of the CCA and CCAS alloys tested at 550 ◦C were smaller, which effectively impeded the movement of dislocations. Therefore, the high-temperature strengths of the CCA and CCAS alloys were higher than that of the CC alloy.

As shown in Figs. 9 and 11, the Ag element was enriched on the precipitates of the CCA and CCAS alloys, promoting the interfacial energy (γCu Cr Ag and γCu Cr Ag Si) lower than that of the CC alloy (γCu Cr) and hindering the coarsening of precipitates.
